verdict: OK to lend in Gurugram auto OEM/dealer chain, but only to BS-VI-compliant, non-Delhi-dependent borrowers; avoid BS-IV fleet-linked and Delhi-border transport exposures.
title: Gurugram Cars & Commercial Vehicles (OEM): a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**An OEM/dealer chain turns steel, components and labour into vehicles, then converts them to cash through dealer inventory and retail finance.** Cash sits in finished-goods inventory and dealer receivables; capex is heavy and lumpy (tooling, paint shop, line upgrades). Pricing power is real but cyclical — peers show margin pressure from commodity and freight costs even as volumes grow [4][7]. **So when a proposal lands, check the split between OEM receivables and dealer inventory; if dealer inventory days are rising while volumes are flat, ask why.**

## What has changed now
**Delhi's BS-VI/BS-IV restrictions have hit roughly 60,000 Gurugram commercial vehicles, with the transport association claiming about 20 per cent of the region's commercial fleet will halt [2][3].** Roads on NH-48 are choked for hours [1]. This is a local demand shock to older-fleet operators, not to new-vehicle OEMs. **So when a proposal lands, check the borrower's fleet vintage and Delhi-NCR route dependence; if more than a fifth of the fleet is pre-BS-VI, ask for a replacement plan before sanction.**

## Where the growth is
**National output for NIC 29 is up 25.2% YoY and 19.2% Apr-to-date [D], and Haryana GST is growing 10.1% versus India's 6.1% [D] — a genuine local tailwind.** Peer results confirm volume strength: M&M auto revenue up 25% with EBIT margin at 9.5% [5]; Tata Motors CV volumes up 26% with price hikes taken [6]. **Pursue BS-VI-compliant OEM component suppliers, new-vehicle dealers and replacement-cycle financiers; avoid BS-IV fleet operators and Delhi-border transport borrowers.**

## How to grow safely
**Bank credit is growing 27.0% against output of 19.2%, a 7.8 pp gap [D] — the system is lending ahead of production, so underwrite to cash flow, not to the cycle.** Structure against dealer receivables and OEM purchase orders, not against fleet value. **Take monthly: GST returns, e-way bills, dealer stock statements and OEM order book; if any of these diverge from the sanction premise, ask for the reconciliation.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for BS-IV fleet write-downs, dealer inventory build and margin squeeze from commodity and freight costs [4][7].** Rating methodology notes leverage and cash-flow cover as the core tests [10][11]. **If a borrower's gearing rises while operating profit falls, treat it as a downgrade trigger, not a temporary dip.**
watch: Monthly GST and e-way bill data
Two consecutive months of falling e-way bills -> ask for order book and re-rate limit
Inventory days rising with flat sales -> ask for OEM discount support and cut exposure
Pre-BS-VI share above 20% -> require replacement plan before renewal
Margin compression with price hikes failing -> ask for pass-through evidence
Gap widening beyond 7.8 pp -> tighten new sanctions to cash-flow-backed only
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
